subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should Discord message permissions become a boolean-or-object configuration contract, and what exact defaults and inheritance rules should apply to legacy booleans, omitted sub-gates, and account overrides?
rationale: This changes a mature security boundary and public configuration surface; source inspection can establish the missing capability but cannot choose whether upgrades preserve every existing permission or tighten destructive operations by default.

options.title: Compatible granular gates
options.body: Retain `messages: boolean` as shorthand and add optional send/read/edit/delete overrides whose omitted values inherit the legacy gate, preserving all existing deployments.

options.title: Explicit separate gates
options.body: Replace the coarse behavior through a doctor migration to four canonical booleans, avoiding a union contract but requiring a defined shipped-config migration.

options.title: Keep coarse gate
options.body: Decline additional configuration complexity and document that Discord message operations intentionally share one trust boundary.

recommendation.title: Compatible granular gates
recommendation.body: Retain `messages: boolean` as shorthand and add optional send/read/edit/delete overrides whose omitted values inherit the legacy gate, preserving all existing deployments.
